standard.name: Independent Bernoulli randomization at probability one half

assumptions.condition: \((U_i,f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\) are independent and identically distributed preassignment draws from a joint law whose \(U_i\)-marginal is \({\rm Uniform}[0,1]\).

standard.name: Li--Wager independent unit-type and response sampling with uniform latent types

assumptions.condition: Conditional on \((U_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the variables \((A_{ij})_{i<j}\) are independent with \(A_{ij}\sim{\rm Bernoulli}(\rho_nW(U_i,U_j))\), \(A_{ji}=A_{ij}\), and \(A_{ii}=0\).
Each \(\psi_k(U_i)\) satisfies Bernstein's moment condition with parameter \(b_\psi\) for \(1\le k\le r\).

standard.name: Li--Wager bounded response and derivative envelope through order two
Known \(C^3\) radius separated from the lower-order response envelope

definitions.name: Li--Wager known-rank \(C^3\) class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}=\{P_{n,d,L}:\text{ every condition in the displayed member-property list holds for }P_{n,d,L}\text{ at triangular-array index }n\}\).  This is the bounded, row-regular, known-rank, two-radius subclass of the Li--Wager sampling family selected by those properties; it is not a claim that the displayed class equals the full class used in LiWager2022RandomGraph.

definitions.name: Li--Wager finite indirect-effect benchmark
definitions.construction: At Bernoulli probability one half, \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}=4n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbb E_Z[Y_i(Z)(M_i-N_i/2)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}]\), equivalently the finite indirect effect in equation (1) of LiWager2022RandomGraph.

definitions.name: Exact realized-degree support correction
definitions.construction: For \(N\ge1\), set \(\delta_N=N^{-1}\) when \(N\) is even and \(\delta_N=(2N)^{-1}\) when \(N\) is odd; for each \(i\) with \(N_i>0\), set \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\).

definitions.name: Exact symmetric discrete local-polynomial score
definitions.construction: For \(N_i>0\), let \(\mu_{2,i}(h)=\mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf 1\{|V_i|\le h_i(h)\}\mid A]\) and \(q_{i,h}=V_i\mathbf 1\{|V_i|\le h_i(h)\}/\mu_{2,i}(h)\). For \(N_i=0\), set \(q_{i,h}=0\) and \(\mu_{2,i}(h)=0\).

definitions.name: Deterministically selected observed principal-component projector
definitions.construction:
Order the eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix \(A\) by decreasing absolute value, breaking equal-absolute-value ties by decreasing signed value.  Within every remaining repeated eigenspace, choose the orthonormal basis obtained by applying Gram--Schmidt to the nonzero vectors in the ordered list of projections of \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) onto that eigenspace.  Let \(\widehat\Psi_r(A)\) contain the first \(r\) resulting orthonormal eigenvectors and define
\[
 \widehat\Pi_r(A)=\widehat\Psi_r(A)\widehat\Psi_r(A)^\top.
\]
This deterministic tie rule makes \(A\mapsto\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) a fixed Borel-measurable sample map.

definitions.name: Explicit first-projection PC handle with bounded-difference certificate
Feasible explicit first-projection PC estimator
definitions.construction:
With the explicit score from \({\rm def:pc-handle}\),
\[
 \widehat\theta_h
 =\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}
 \left[q_{i,h}-4\left\{\widehat\Pi_r(A)A
       (Z-\tfrac12\mathbf1_n)\right\}_i\right]Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]

definitions.name: Graph-observable degree-exact radii for the explicit PC handle
definitions.construction:
For the explicit certificates in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\), set
\[
 \overline b_h(A)=\frac{L}{6n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}h_i(h)^2
 +\frac{B}{n}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}
 +\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
\]
and
\[
 \overline s_h(A)^2=\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}.
\]
Thus \(\overline s_h(A)\) is a finite-sample conditional standard-deviation certificate, not an asserted sharp-rate formula.

definitions.name: Supported and degree-exact full-class envelopes
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}=\sqrt{d/n}+\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}\{Lh^2+(n\sqrt d\,h^3)^{-1/2}\}\) and \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}=\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[\overline b_{h^\dagger}(A)+\overline s_{h^\dagger}(A)]\).

definitions.name: Absolute-risk and honest-length criteria
definitions.construction: \(R^*_{n,d,L}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\theta-\theta_n|\) and \(\Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)=\inf_{\mathcal C:\,\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P(\theta_n\in\mathcal C)\ge1-\alpha}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C)]\), where the infima range over measurable procedures based on \((A,Z,(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i\in\mathcal V_n})\).

statements.statement: For every \(i\in\mathcal V_n\) with \(N_i\ge1\) and every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\), the exact support correction gives \(\mu_{2,i}(h)>0\). Symmetry of \(M_i\sim{\rm Binomial}(N_i,1/2)\) yields \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}\mid A]=0\), \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i\mid A]=1\), \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]=0\), and \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}^2\mid A]=\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}\). For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(|\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}f_i(a,1/2+V_i)\mid A]-\partial_xf_i(a,1/2)|\le Lh_i(h)^2/6\).
statements.justification: This establishes exact derivative moments at every positive realized degree and removes the zero-normalizer failure at the lower bandwidth endpoint.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph uses an unlocalized global binomial score; ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest does not face a random degree lattice.
statements.consumer: It supplies the unitwise bias and exact inverse-moment contribution in the feasible-PC certificate.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(i\in\mathcal V_n\) with \(N_i=N\geq1\), fix \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\), and condition on \(A\) and the preassignment response functions.  By \({\rm ass:bernoulli-design}\),
\[
 M_i\mid A\sim {\rm Binomial}(N,1/2),\qquad V_i=M_i/N-1/2.
\]
If \(N\) is even, the nearest nonzero exposure-lattice points are \(\pm N^{-1}\); if \(N\) is odd, they are \(\pm(2N)^{-1}\).  Each has strictly positive binomial probability.  Hence \({\rm def:lattice-radius}\) implies
\[
 \Pr_Z\{0<|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\mid A\}>0,
\]
and the nonnegative summands in \({\rm def:discrete-score}\) give \(\mu_{2,i}(h)>0\).

The involution \(M_i\mapsto N-M_i\) preserves binomial probability and sends \(V_i\) to \(-V_i\).  The truncation indicator is even and \(q_{i,h}\) is odd.  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}\mid A]=0,
\]
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i\mid A]
 =\frac{\mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]}{\mu_{2,i}(h)}=1,
\]
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]
 =\frac{\mathbb E_Z[V_i^3\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]}{\mu_{2,i}(h)}=0,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}^2\mid A]
 =\frac{\mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]}{\mu_{2,i}(h)^2}
 =\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}.
\]
Every division here is valid by the strict positivity just proved.

Fix \(a\in\{0,1\}\).  Taylor's formula with integral remainder, together with \({\rm ass:third-derivative-bound}\), gives for \(v\in[-1/2,1/2]\)
\[
 f_i(a,1/2+v)=f_i(a,1/2)+\partial_xf_i(a,1/2)v
 +\frac12\partial_x^2f_i(a,1/2)v^2+R_i(a,v),
 \qquad |R_i(a,v)|\leq \frac L6|v|^3.
\]
Multiplication by \(q_{i,h}\), conditional expectation, and the three preceding moment identities show
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}f_i(a,1/2+V_i)\mid A]-\partial_xf_i(a,1/2)
 =\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}R_i(a,V_i)\mid A].
\]
On the support of \(q_{i,h}\), \(|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\).  Consequently
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \left|\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}R_i(a,V_i)\mid A]\right|
 &\leq \frac{L}{6\mu_{2,i}(h)}
 \mathbb E_Z[|V_i|^4\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]\\
 &\leq \frac{Lh_i(h)^2}{6\mu_{2,i}(h)}
 \mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]
 =\frac L6h_i(h)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves all claimed moment and bias identities.

statements.statement: Conditional on \(A\) and \((f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the new derivative target and the Li--Wager finite indirect effect satisfy \( |\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n|\le L(8n)^{-1}\sum_{i:N_i>0}N_i^{-1}+Bn^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf 1\{N_i=0\}\). Consequently, in the degree regime of LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem 6, this difference is \(o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n})\), so their Gaussian theorem is an asymptotic benchmark for \(\theta_n\), not a finite-sample same-target result.
statements.justification: The bridge states exactly when the published finite indirect effect and the finite-population derivative are asymptotically interchangeable.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph Proposition 1 gives a minimum-degree approximation; the displayed degree-exact symmetric remainder keeps isolates visible and does not identify the two finite-sample targets.
statements.consumer: It permits valid asymptotic comparison with Theorem 6 while keeping the proposed finite-population derivative as a distinct target.
statements.proof_tex:
Work first conditionally on \(A\) and \((f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), and define the proof-intermediate function
\[
g_i(x):=\frac{f_i(1,x)+f_i(0,x)}{2},\qquad x\in[0,1].
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-design}\), conditional on \((U_i,f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\) and \(A\), every assignment vector has probability \(2^{-n}\).  This probability does not depend on the latent types.  The conditional-expectation identity
\[
\Pr\!\left(Z=z\mid A,(f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\right)
=\mathbb E\!\left[
\Pr\!\left(Z=z\mid A,(U_i,f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\right)
\mathrel{\big|}A,(f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}
\right]
=2^{-n}
\]
therefore shows that the assignment remains product Bernoulli conditional on \(A\) and the response functions.

Fix \(i\in\mathcal V_n\) with \(N_i=m>0\).  Because \(A_{ii}=0\), \(M_i\) is a function only of \((Z_j)_{j\ne i}\).  Hence \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-design}\) gives
\[
M_i\sim {\rm Binomial}(m,1/2)
\quad\text{and}\quad
Z_i\ \text{is independent of}\ M_i
\]
under the conditional law just obtained.  Define the unit-level contribution
\[
\beta_i:=4\,\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
Y_i(Z)(M_i-m/2)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}
\right].
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:anonymous-interference}\), \(Y_i(Z)=f_i(Z_i,1/2+V_i)\) for this nonisolated unit.  Averaging first over the independent variable \(Z_i\) replaces this outcome by \(g_i(1/2+V_i)\), while the definition of \(V_i\) gives \(M_i-m/2=mV_i\).  Consequently,
\[
\beta_i
=4m\,\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
g_i(1/2+V_i)V_i\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}
\right].
\]
If \(N_i=0\), then \(M_i-N_i/2=0\), so set \(\beta_i=0\).  The construction in \(\texttt{def:li-wager-target}\) now yields
\[
\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}=\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\beta_i.
\]

For the fixed nonisolated unit, let \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) be independent random variables taking the values \(-1/2\) and \(1/2\) with equal probability, and put \(S_m=\sum_{j=1}^mX_j\).  The preceding binomial law shows that \(V_i\) has the law of \(S_m/m\).  Centering and independence give
\[
\mathbb E S_m^2=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbb E X_j^2=\frac m4,
\qquad
\mathbb E S_m^3=0.
\]
In the fourth-power expansion, the only terms with nonzero expectation are the one-index terms and the terms consisting of two pairs.  Since \(\mathbb E X_j^2=1/4\) and \(\mathbb E X_j^4=1/16\),
\[
\mathbb E S_m^4
=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbb E X_j^4
+6\sum_{1\le j<k\le m}\mathbb E X_j^2\mathbb E X_k^2
=\frac{3m^2-2m}{16}.
\]
Thus
\[
\mathbb E V_i=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E V_i^2=\frac1{4m},
\qquad
\mathbb E V_i^3=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E V_i^4=\frac{3m^2-2m}{16m^4}\le\frac3{16m^2}.
\]

By \(\texttt{ass:third-derivative-bound}\) and the definition of \(g_i\),
\[
\sup_{x\in[0,1]}\left|g_i^{(3)}(x)\right|\le L.
\]
Repeated use of the fundamental theorem of calculus on the segment joining \(1/2\) and \(1/2+v\), which is contained in \([0,1]\) for \(v\in[-1/2,1/2]\), gives
\[
g_i(1/2+v)
=g_i(1/2)+g_i'(1/2)v+\frac12g_i''(1/2)v^2+R_i(v),
\qquad
|R_i(v)|\le\frac L6|v|^3.
\]
Multiplying by \(v\), taking the conditional expectation, and using the four moment identities above makes the constant and quadratic Taylor terms vanish and gives \(4m\mathbb E V_i^2=1\).  Therefore
\[
\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)
=4m\,\mathbb E\!\left[V_iR_i(V_i)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}\right],
\]
and hence
\[
\left|\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)\right|
\le \frac{4mL}{6}\mathbb E V_i^4
\le \frac{4mL}{6}\frac3{16m^2}
=\frac{L}{8m}.
\]
By \(\texttt{def:target}\), the contribution of unit \(i\) to \(\theta_n\) is \(g_i'(1/2)\).  For an isolated unit, \(\texttt{ass:response-envelope}\) gives
\[
|g_i'(1/2)|
\le\frac{|\partial_xf_i(1,1/2)|+|\partial_xf_i(0,1/2)|}{2}
\le B.
\]
Separating the nonisolated and isolated vertices and applying the triangle inequality proves the asserted finite-sample bound:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n\right|
&\le \frac1n\sum_{i:N_i>0}\left|\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)\right|
+\frac1n\sum_{i:N_i=0}|g_i'(1/2)|\\
&\le \frac{L}{8n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}
+\frac Bn\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

We also derive an auxiliary bound that avoids imposing any asymptotic restriction on \(L\).  By \(\texttt{ass:response-envelope}\), \(\sup_x|g_i''(x)|\le B\).  The first-order Taylor identity obtained from the fundamental theorem of calculus is
\[
g_i(1/2+v)=g_i(1/2)+g_i'(1/2)v+T_i(v),
\qquad
|T_i(v)|\le\frac B2v^2.
\]
The same moment cancellation as above and the power-mean inequality give
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)|
&\le 2mB\,\mathbb E|V_i|^3
\le 2mB\,(\mathbb E V_i^4)^{3/4}\\
&\le 2mB\left(\frac3{16m^2}\right)^{3/4}
=\frac{3^{3/4}B}{4\sqrt m}.
\end{aligned}
\]

It remains to establish the asymptotic comparison.  Consider a triangular-array sequence satisfying the proposition's assumptions and the degree regime of LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem~6.  The envelope \(B\) and regularity constant \(\kappa\) are fixed class constants.  By \(\texttt{lem:li-wager-theorem-six-regime}\),
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log\rho_n}{\log n}>-\frac12.
\]
Choose \(\varepsilon>0\) strictly smaller than the gap between this lower limit and \(-1/2\).  Then, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\rho_n\ge n^{-1/2+\varepsilon}.
\]
The accompanying upper exponent condition in \(\texttt{lem:li-wager-theorem-six-regime}\), consistently with \(\texttt{ass:sparse-limit}\), places the sequence in the sparse regime; the displayed lower bound is the part needed below.
Also, \(0\le W\le\kappa\) from \(\texttt{ass:kernel-bound}\) and \(\kappa\ge1\) imply \(\min\{1,W(u,v)\}\ge W(u,v)/\kappa\).  Therefore \(\texttt{ass:degree-regularity}\) gives the essential-infimum bound
\[
\mathop{\rm ess\,inf}_{u\in[0,1]}\int_0^1\min\{1,W(u,v)\}\,dv\ge\kappa^{-2}.
\]
If the theorem's pointwise-infimum convention is used, let \(E\) be the null exceptional set and replace \(W(u,v)\) by \(\kappa^{-1}\) whenever \(u\in E\) or \(v\in E\).  This symmetric modification changes \(W\) only on a null subset of \([0,1]^2\), hence leaves the sampled law unchanged because the latent types are uniform by \(\texttt{ass:unit-sampling}\), and it makes every exceptional-row integral at least \(\kappa^{-1}\).  Thus an equivalent representative satisfies the row-regularity condition recorded in \(\texttt{lem:li-wager-theorem-six-regime}\).

Fix a vertex \(i\).  By the independent uniform latent types in \(\texttt{ass:unit-sampling}\) and conditional edge independence in \(\texttt{ass:graphon-draw}\), after conditioning only on \(U_i=u\), the pairs consisting of \(U_j\) and the edge draw \(A_{ij}\), for \(j\ne i\), are independent and identically distributed.  Marginalizing each \(U_j\) therefore gives
\[
N_i\mid U_i=u\sim {\rm Binomial}(n-1,p_n(u)),
\qquad
p_n(u):=\rho_n\int_0^1W(u,v)\,dv.
\]
The conditions \(\texttt{ass:kernel-bound}\) and \(\texttt{ass:edge-probability}\) imply \(0\le p_n(u)\le\rho_n\kappa\le1\).  Moreover, \(\texttt{ass:degree-regularity}\) gives, for almost every \(u\),
\[
\mu_i(u):=\mathbb E[N_i\mid U_i=u]
=(n-1)p_n(u)
\ge\frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{\kappa}.
\]
Because every \(U_i\) is uniform by \(\texttt{ass:unit-sampling}\), this almost-everywhere inequality applies to all of the finitely many realized types with probability one at each \(n\).

For completeness, derive the required binomial lower-tail estimate.  If \(S\sim{\rm Binomial}(m,p)\), \(\mu=mp\), and \(t=\log2\), then on \(\{S\le\mu/2\}\) one has \(e^{-tS}\ge e^{-t\mu/2}\).  Markov's inequality and \(1-y\le e^{-y}\) consequently give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Pr(S\le\mu/2)
&\le e^{t\mu/2}\mathbb E e^{-tS}
=e^{t\mu/2}(1-p+pe^{-t})^m\\
&\le\exp\!\left\{\frac{t\mu}{2}-\mu(1-e^{-t})\right\}
=\exp\!\left\{-\frac{1-\log2}{2}\mu\right\}
\le e^{-\mu/8},
\end{aligned}
\]
where the last step uses \((1-\log2)/2\ge1/8\).  Since \(\mu_i(u)\ge(n-1)\rho_n/\kappa\), the event
\[
\left\{N_i<\frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{2\kappa}\right\}
\]
is contained in \(\{N_i<\mu_i(u)/2\}\).  Applying the preceding estimate conditionally on \(U_i\), integrating over \(U_i\), and taking a union bound yield, for
\[
\mathcal E_n:=\left\{\min_{i\in\mathcal V_n}N_i
\ge\frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{2\kappa}\right\},
\]
the probability bound
\[
\Pr(\mathcal E_n^c)
\le n\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{8\kappa}\right\}
\longrightarrow0.
\]
Indeed, the exponent diverges at least as a fixed multiple of \(n^{1/2+\varepsilon}\), which dominates \(\log n\).

On \(\mathcal E_n\) there are no isolated vertices and
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\frac1{\sqrt{N_i}}
\le\left(\frac{2\kappa}{(n-1)\rho_n}\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The auxiliary response-envelope bound thus implies
\[
\frac{\left|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n\right|}{\sqrt{\rho_n}}
\le\frac{3^{3/4}B\sqrt{2\kappa}}{4\sqrt{n-1}\,\rho_n}
\le\frac{3^{3/4}B\sqrt{2\kappa}}{4\sqrt{1-1/n}\,n^{\varepsilon}}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{on }\mathcal E_n.
\]
Together with \(\Pr(\mathcal E_n^c)\to0\), this proves
\[
\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n=o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n}).
\]
Finally, \(\texttt{lem:li-wager-theorem-six-regime}\) records that the published principal-component-balancing Gaussian result uses the same \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\) scale and is centered at \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}\).  The last display proves asymptotic equivalence of that center and \(\theta_n\) on precisely this scale.  In contrast, the nonzero degree-exact finite-sample remainder proved above shows that the two targets were not made equal by definition.  This establishes the stated benchmark interpretation.

statements.statement:
At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\), let \(h=h^\dagger\).  The feasible estimator and interval in \({\rm def:estimator}\) and \({\rm def:honest-interval}\) satisfy \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_{h^\dagger}-\theta_n|\le\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\), \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_{h^\dagger}\}\ge1-\alpha\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{h^\dagger})]
 \le2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\]
Before intersection with \([-B,B]\), the pointwise half-length is exactly \(\overline b_{h^\dagger}(A)+\overline s_{h^\dagger}(A)/\sqrt\alpha\), including every realized degree and isolate.  No comparison of \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\) with \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\) is asserted.
statements.justification: This theorem gives exact finite-sample risk, coverage, and expected-length inequalities in terms of the observable radius envelope.
statements.gap: No theorem compares the conservative observable envelope with the analytic supported envelope, so this is not a sharp rate result.
statements.consumer: Experimenters can report the realized interval safely and treat a wide certificate as evidence for an ego-cluster follow-up.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\).  Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), put
\[
 \mathcal G=\sigma\!\left(A,(f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\right),
 \qquad E_h=\widehat\theta_h-\theta_n,
 \qquad m_h=\mathbb E_P(E_h\mid\mathcal G).
\tag{1}
\]
The minimizer in \({\rm def:exact-optimal-bandwidth}\) exists.  Indeed, across all possible degrees, the finite-lattice score and certificates in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\) have finitely many bandwidth breakpoints.  On every interval beginning at one of its included breakpoints they are constant, apart from the Taylor term, which is continuous and nondecreasing.  The supremum over \(P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) is also nondecreasing on that interval, so the interval minimum is attained at its included left endpoint.  There are finitely many such endpoints in the nonempty compact interval \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\).  Thus a global minimum is attained, its smallest minimizer \(h^\dagger\) is well defined, and it is fixed by the class rather than by the realized sample.

By \({\rm thm:explicit-pc-conditional-certificate}\),
\[
 |m_h|\leq\overline b_h(A),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P\{(E_h-m_h)^2\mid\mathcal G\}\leq\overline s_h(A)^2.
\tag{2}
\]
Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz and (2) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_P(|E_h|\mid\mathcal G)
 \leq |m_h|+\{\mathbb E_P((E_h-m_h)^2\mid\mathcal G)\}^{1/2}
 \leq\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A).
\tag{3}
\]
Taking expectations, setting \(h=h^\dagger\), taking the class supremum, and applying \({\rm def:frontier-envelope}\) yields
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_{h^\dagger}-\theta_n|
 \leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\tag{4}
\]

Conditional Chebyshev applied to (2) gives
\[
 P\!\left(|E_h-m_h|>\overline s_h(A)/\sqrt\alpha\mid\mathcal G\right)\leq\alpha,
\tag{5}
\]
with a zero left side when \(\overline s_h(A)=0\).  The triangle inequality and \(|m_h|\leq\overline b_h(A)\) turn (5) into coverage by the untruncated interval.  Moreover, \({\rm ass:response-envelope}\) and \({\rm def:target}\) give \(|\theta_n|\leq B\), so intersection with \([-B,B]\) cannot remove \(\theta_n\).  Integrating and setting \(h=h^\dagger\) proves
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_{h^\dagger}\}\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{6}
\]

Before intersection, \({\rm def:honest-interval}\) has half-length exactly \(\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)/\sqrt\alpha\).  Intersection only shortens it, and therefore
\[
 \operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_h)
 \leq2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\{\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)\}.
\tag{7}
\]
Taking expectations and the class supremum at \(h=h^\dagger\), then using \({\rm def:frontier-envelope}\), proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{h^\dagger})]
 \leq2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\tag{8}
\]
The sums in \({\rm def:radii}\) explicitly retain every positive realized degree and every isolate.  Equations (4), (6), and (8) prove the theorem; none compares \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\) with \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\).

statements.statement:
For \(1\leq k\leq r\), let \(I_k=[(k-1)/r,k/r)\), with \(1\) included in \(I_r\), put \(\psi_k(u)=\sqrt r\,\mathbf 1\{u\in I_k\}\), and set
\[
 c_0=\max\{r/\kappa,r\underline\lambda\},
 \qquad
 W_0(u,v)=c_0\mathbf 1\{u\text{ and }v\text{ belong to the same }I_k\}.
\]
Suppose, in addition to the conditions defining \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), that
\[
 c_0\leq\kappa,
 \qquad
 b_\psi\geq (r-1)/\sqrt r.
\]
Let \(s_0=B/4\), let \(\xi_i\) be i.i.d. with density \(p_{s_0}(t)=s_0^{-1}\cos^2(\pi t/(2s_0))\mathbf 1\{|t|\leq s_0\}\), and use response pairs \(f_i^\pm(a,x)=\xi_i\pm g(x)\), with the three functions \(g\) constructed in the proof.  Then \(W_0\) and these random-intercept response laws generate an explicit block submodel of \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\).  Along sequences with \(B,L,r,\kappa,\underline\lambda,b_\psi,\alpha,C_{\log}\) fixed and \(C_{\log}\log n\leq d=o(n)\), there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(n\) and \(d\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
Within this same block submodel, respectively, a degree-lattice bump, an interior \(C^3\) bump, and a linear response pair furnish the lattice term, the interior nonlinear term for both absolute risk and honest expected length, and the graph floor.  The two displayed compatibility inequalities are only sufficient conditions for this explicit block witness and do not characterize nonemptiness; \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) separately proves the same supported lower benchmark over every eventually nonempty repaired class.
statements.justification: The explicit equal-block graphon and three same-class response pairs prove the supported analytic converse under the displayed sufficient compatibility conditions; \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) separately proves the same benchmark over every eventually nonempty repaired class.
statements.gap: The compatibility inequalities are merely sufficient for this explicit block witness and do not characterize nonemptiness. This is a limitation of the witness, not a gap in the supported lower benchmark, which \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) establishes over every eventually nonempty repaired class.
statements.consumer: Experimenters may use the supported bandwidth envelope as a certified global lower benchmark whenever the repaired class is eventually nonempty; this theorem additionally provides a concrete equal-block witness when its displayed compatibility conditions hold.

statements.statement:
For \(L>0\), at every sufficiently large triangular-array index the supported-unit component satisfies \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp Ld^{-2}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\leq d^{-1}\), \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), and \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\geq d^{-1/2}\).  At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\), the explicit degree-exact procedure proves
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
 \leq2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\]
Along every sequence covered by the unrestricted supported converse, there is a constant \(c>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
Every graph-only conditional-bias certificate over the repaired class retains at least \(Bn^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}\) on a realized graph.  No bound \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\lesssim\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\) is proved; hence the three analytic phases are a tuning geometry and a minimax lower benchmark, not an achieved honest expected-length frontier.
statements.justification: This proposition proves the bandwidth optimization and the honest lower--upper bracket without calling the conservative upper envelope sharp.
statements.gap: The bounded-difference certificate has no proved comparison with the analytic supported envelope, so tightness of the displayed bracket remains unresolved.
statements.consumer: The three phases are useful for design triage as lower-benchmark geometry, not as a guaranteed confidence-length curve.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume \(L>0\), and write
\[
 c_{n,d}=n^{-1/2}d^{-1/4},
 \qquad
 g(h)=Lh^2+c_{n,d}h^{-3/2},
 \qquad
 \ell=d^{-1},
 \qquad
 u=d^{-1/2}.
\tag{64}
\]
By \({\rm ass:log-degree}\), \(d\to\infty\), so at every sufficiently large index \(d\ge4\) and \({\rm def:bandwidth-set}\) gives \(\mathcal H_{n,d}=[\ell,u]\).  From \({\rm def:optimal-bandwidth}\),
\[
 h_0^7=\frac{L^{-2}}{n\sqrt d}.
\tag{65}
\]
Since \(c_{n,d}^2=(n\sqrt d)^{-1}\), positive square roots in (65) give
\[
 Lh_0^2=c_{n,d}h_0^{-3/2}.
\tag{66}
\]

If \(h_0\leq\ell\), then \(g(h)\geq L\ell^2\) for every \(h\in[\ell,u]\), while monotonicity and (66) give
\[
 c_{n,d}\ell^{-3/2}
 \leq c_{n,d}h_0^{-3/2}
 =Lh_0^2\leq L\ell^2.
\tag{67}
\]
Evaluation at \(\ell\) proves
\[
 Ld^{-2}\leq\inf_{h\in[\ell,u]}g(h)\leq2Ld^{-2}.
\tag{68}
\]
If \(\ell<h_0<u\), then for \(h\geq h_0\) the first term of \(g(h)\) is at least \(Lh_0^2\), and for \(h\leq h_0\) its second term is at least \(c_{n,d}h_0^{-3/2}=Lh_0^2\).  Evaluation at \(h_0\) gives
\[
 Lh_0^2\leq\inf_{h\in[\ell,u]}g(h)\leq2Lh_0^2,
 \qquad
 Lh_0^2=L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{69}
\]
If \(h_0\geq u\), then
\[
 g(h)\geq c_{n,d}u^{-3/2}=\sqrt{d/n}
\tag{70}
\]
for every admissible \(h\), while (66) and \(u\leq h_0\) imply \(Lu^2\leq c_{n,d}u^{-3/2}\).  Evaluation at \(u\) yields
\[
 \sqrt{d/n}\leq\inf_{h\in[\ell,u]}g(h)\leq2\sqrt{d/n}.
\tag{71}
\]
By \({\rm def:frontier-envelope}\),
\[
 \mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}
 =\sqrt{d/n}+\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}g(h).
\tag{72}
\]
Adding \(\sqrt{d/n}\) to (68)--(71) proves the three asserted analytic equivalences.

At every index with nonempty bandwidth set, \({\rm thm:honest-upper}\) supplies a measurable estimator with worst-case absolute risk at most \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\), and an interval meeting the uniform coverage constraint with worst-case expected length at most \(2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\).  Inserting these procedures into the infima in \({\rm def:minimax-criteria}\) gives
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
 \leq2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\tag{73}
\]
Along every sequence satisfying the hypotheses of \({\rm thm:unrestricted-supported-converse}\), that theorem, now proved while retaining the independent uniform latent types and the original admissible kernel, gives a constant \(c>0\) such that
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}
\tag{74}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Finally, \({\rm thm:conditional-isolate-wall}\) proves pointwise that every graph-only conditional-bias radius over the same class satisfies
\[
 b(A)\geq\frac Bn\sum_i\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}.
\tag{75}
\]
Equations (68)--(75) prove the analytic phases and the honest bracket
\[
 c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}
 \leq R^*_{n,d,L}\leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}
 \leq\Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
 \leq2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\tag{76}
\]
Neither \({\rm def:radii}\) nor \({\rm thm:honest-upper}\) supplies \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\lesssim\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\).  Therefore the three phases are a tuning geometry and minimax lower benchmark, not an achieved honest expected-length frontier, exactly as asserted.

statements.statement:
On the predeclared sharp-radius class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\subseteq\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), evaluate \({\rm def:radii}\) and \({\rm def:optimal-bandwidth}\) at \(L=0\).  Then \(h_0=\infty\), \(h_\star=d^{-1/2}\), and the positive-degree Taylor term in \(\overline b_{h_\star}(A)\) is identically zero.  The exact moment equation \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]=0\) also cancels every quadratic exposure response, with affine responses as a special case.  At \(h_\star=d^{-1/2}\), the analytic nonremainder score and graph terms both have order \(\sqrt{d/n}\), while the complete corrected certificate is
\[
 \overline b_{h_\star}(A)=\frac Bn\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}+\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h_\star},
 \qquad
 \overline s_{h_\star}(A)^2=\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h_\star}
 =\frac1{4n^2}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V_n}
 \left(\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\beta_{ij,h_\star}\right)^2.
\]
No sharp stochastic order is asserted for the last display.  An affine realized law inside \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) with \(L>0\) does not permit setting the honesty radius to zero; the reduction applies only when \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\) is fixed before observing the experiment.
statements.justification: On the prespecified zero-radius class, every exposure response is quadratic and the exact discrete moments eliminate its positive-degree approximation error.
statements.gap: The corrected bounded-difference variance radius remains explicit but has no sharp stochastic order, even in this zero-radius reduction.
statements.consumer: Analysts may use the largest admissible bandwidth only when the zero-radius class was fixed before outcomes were observed.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a law in the prespecified class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\).  By \({\rm ass:third-derivative-bound}\) with radius zero, \(\partial_x^3f_i(a,x)=0\) for every displayed argument.  Since each response is \(C^3\), the fundamental theorem of calculus gives, for \(x,y\in[0,1]\),
\[
 \partial_x^2f_i(a,x)-\partial_x^2f_i(a,y)
 =\int_y^x\partial_t^3f_i(a,t)\,dt=0.
\]
Thus the second derivative is constant and two further integrations show that \(x\mapsto f_i(a,x)\) is a polynomial of degree at most two.

Substitution of \(L=0\) into \({\rm def:optimal-bandwidth}\) gives
\[
 h_0=\infty,
 \qquad h_\star=\min\{d^{-1/2},\max\{d^{-1},\infty\}\}=d^{-1/2}.
\tag{1}
\]
The logarithmic-degree condition in \({\rm def:model-class}\) implies \(d\to\infty\), so for all sufficiently large indices \(d^{-1}\leq d^{-1/2}\leq1/2\); hence (1) belongs to \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\).  The positive-degree Taylor term in \({\rm def:radii}\) is multiplied by \(L\) and is therefore zero.

Fix \(i\) with \(N_i>0\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).  By \({\rm lem:exact-score-moments}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}\mid A]=0,
 \qquad \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i\mid A]=1,
 \qquad \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]=0.
\tag{2}
\]
The exact quadratic expansion and (2) give
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}f_i(a,1/2+V_i)\mid A]=\partial_xf_i(a,1/2),
\tag{3}
\]
so every quadratic response, and in particular every affine response, has zero positive-degree approximation error.

At \(h_\star=d^{-1/2}\), the analytic stochastic term in \({\rm def:frontier-envelope}\) is
\[
 (n\sqrt d\,h_\star^3)^{-1/2}
 =(n\sqrt d\,d^{-3/2})^{-1/2}=\sqrt{d/n},
\tag{4}
\]
and the graph term is also \(\sqrt{d/n}\).  Direct substitution of \(L=0\) and \(h=h_\star\) into \({\rm def:pc-handle}\) and \({\rm def:radii}\) yields
\[
 \overline b_{h_\star}(A)
 =\frac Bn\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}
 +\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h_\star},
\tag{5}
\]
\[
 \overline s_{h_\star}(A)^2
 =\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h_\star}
 =\frac1{4n^2}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V_n}
 \left(\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\beta_{ij,h_\star}\right)^2.
\tag{6}
\]
The certification in \({\rm thm:explicit-pc-conditional-certificate}\) makes (5)--(6) the complete conditional certificates; no asymptotic order for (6) is used.

All member properties other than the third-derivative radius are unchanged when the radius is reduced from \(L\) to zero, so \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\subseteq\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\).  To verify the claimed non-post-hoc qualification when \(L>0\), retain the graph and uniform latent-type law of an admissible member and set deterministically
\[
 g(a,x)=c(x-1/2)^3,
 \qquad c=\frac12\min\{B/3,L/6\}>0.
\tag{7}
\]
This preserves unit sampling, randomization, the graph law, and anonymous interference.  Moreover,
\[
 \|g\|_\infty\leq c/8,\quad
 \|\partial_xg\|_\infty\leq3c/4,\quad
 \|\partial_x^2g\|_\infty\leq3c,\quad
 \|\partial_x^3g\|_\infty=6c,
\]
which are bounded by \(B,B,B,L\), respectively.  Thus this alternative lies in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) but not in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\).  For \(N_i>0\),
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}g(a,1/2+V_i)\mid A]
 =c\frac{\mathbb E_Z[V_i^4\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]}{\mu_{2,i}(h)}>0.
\tag{8}
\]
The denominator is positive by \({\rm lem:exact-score-moments}\), and the numerator is positive because the truncation contains a nearest nonzero lattice point of positive binomial mass.  Hence a realized affine law inside the positive-radius class cannot justify replacing the prespecified honesty class by the zero-radius class.  Equations (1)--(8) prove the proposition.

statements.statement:
For the explicit construction in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\), all distinct scores over \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\) can be represented and computed in polynomial time.  Conditional on \(A\) and the preassignment response functions, for every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\),
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z(\widehat\theta_h-\theta_n\mid A,(f_i)_i)\right|
 \leq\overline b_h(A),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_Z(\widehat\theta_h\mid A,(f_i)_i)
 \leq\overline s_h(A)^2.
\]
Consequently \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_h\}\geq1-\alpha\).  If \(C_A=\widehat\Pi_r(A)A\) and
\[
 G_A(C_A)=\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j:A_{ij}=1}(C_A)_{ij}^2,
\]
then the explicit bias certificate also satisfies the deterministic bound
\[
 \widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
 \leq \frac{2B}{n}\|C_A\|_*
      +B\sqrt{\frac{G_A(C_A)}{n}}.
\]
The exact first two Hoeffding projections create no bandwidth-dependent term.  This result does not assert the sharper uniform rates \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}=O_P(d/n)\) and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}=O_P(d/n)\); the displayed graph norm and conservative variance certificate are the proved computable quantities under the frozen assumptions.
statements.justification: This gives an explicit polynomial-time first-projection PC estimator and a finite-sample conditional certificate without asserting the unproved sharp spectral remainder rates.
statements.gap: The exact first two Hoeffding projections are benign, but the frozen assumptions do not yet yield the edge-restricted projector norm and sharp product-ANOVA bounds needed for a \(d/n\) variance remainder.
statements.consumer: The observable certificate is safe for experiment reporting; its conservative variance term transparently signals that the sharp confidence-length frontier remains unresolved.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(A\), the preassignment response functions, and \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\).  All expectations and variances below are over the independent assignment coordinates from \({\rm ass:bernoulli-design}\).  Put
\[
 X=Z-\frac12\mathbf1_n,\qquad P_A=\widehat\Pi_r(A),\qquad C_A=P_AA,
 \qquad F_h(Z)=\widehat\theta_h.
\]

We first prove the variance certificate.  If \(z^{(j)}\) is obtained from \(z\) by flipping coordinate \(j\), the finite maximum in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\) gives
\[
 |q_{i,h}(z)-q_{i,h}(z^{(j)})|\leq D_{ij,h}.
\tag{1}
\]
Indeed, the difference is zero when \(A_{ij}=0\); when \(A_{ij}=1\), the treated-neighbor count moves between two consecutive integers appearing in that maximum.  The normalizer is positive for \(N_i>0\) by \({\rm lem:exact-score-moments}\).  Since \(|X_j|=1/2\), the definitions of \(Q_{i,h}\), \(\Gamma_{i,h}\), and \(\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}\) give
\[
 |\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}(z)|\leq Q_{i,h}+2\sum_{j'}|(C_A)_{ij'}|=\Gamma_{i,h},
\tag{2}
\]
and, because a flip changes \(X_j\) by one in absolute value,
\[
 |\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}(z)-\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}(z^{(j)})|
 \leq D_{ij,h}+4|(C_A)_{ij}|.
\tag{3}
\]

The response-level part of \({\rm ass:response-envelope}\) gives \(|Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}(z)|\leq B\).  If \(j=i\), a flip changes only the own-treatment argument, so the two response values differ by at most \(2B\).  If \(A_{ij}=1\), then \(j\ne i\), the exposure fraction changes by \(N_i^{-1}\), and the derivative envelope plus the fundamental theorem of calculus bounds the change by \(B/N_i\).  Otherwise anonymous interference makes it zero.  With the convention in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\),
\[
 |Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}(z)-Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}(z^{(j)})|
 \leq B\left\{2\mathbf1\{i=j\}+\frac{A_{ij}}{N_i}\right\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Applying \(|gy-g'y'|\leq|g-g'||y|+|g'||y-y'|\) to (2)--(4) proves
\[
 |\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}(z)Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}(z)
 -\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}(z^{(j)})Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}(z^{(j)})|
 \leq\beta_{ij,h}.
\tag{5}
\]
Summation and \({\rm def:estimator}\) yield
\[
 |F_h(z)-F_h(z^{(j)})|
 \leq c_{j,h}:=n^{-1}\sum_i\beta_{ij,h}.
\tag{6}
\]

For completeness, let \(\mathcal F_j=\sigma(Z_1,\ldots,Z_j)\), \(M_j=\mathbb E_Z(F_h\mid\mathcal F_j)\), and \(E_j=M_j-M_{j-1}\).  Martingale differences are orthogonal, so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_Z(F_h)=\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbb E_ZE_j^2.
\tag{7}
\]
Given \(\mathcal F_{j-1}\), the difference between the two values of \(M_j\) obtained by setting \(Z_j=1\) and \(Z_j=0\) is an average over future coordinates of differences bounded by (6), hence is at most \(c_{j,h}\).  A two-point variable with equal masses and range at most \(c_{j,h}\) has variance at most \(c_{j,h}^2/4\).  Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_Z(\widehat\theta_h\mid A,(f_i)_i)
 \leq\frac14\sum_jc_{j,h}^2
 =\frac1{4n^2}\sum_j\left(\sum_i\beta_{ij,h}\right)^2
 =\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}=\overline s_h(A)^2.
\tag{8}
\]

We next prove the bias certificate.  For \(N_i>0\), \(q_{i,h}\) depends only on neighbor assignments and is independent of \(Z_i\).  Conditioning first on \(Z_i=a\), applying \({\rm ass:anonymous-interference}\) and \({\rm lem:exact-score-moments}\), and averaging the two equiprobable own-treatment values gives
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}]
 -\frac{\partial_xf_i(1,1/2)+\partial_xf_i(0,1/2)}2\right|
 \leq\frac L6h_i(h)^2.
\tag{9}
\]
For \(N_i=0\), \(q_{i,h}=0\), while the derivative envelope bounds the absolute target contribution by \(B\).  Thus the score part has conditional bias at most
\[
 \frac{L}{6n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}h_i(h)^2
 +\frac Bn\sum_i\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}.
\tag{10}
\]

It remains to bound the PC subtraction.  Centering and \(|Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}|\leq B\) imply
\[
 |\mathbb E_Z[X_iY_i^{\mathrm{obs}}]|\leq B/2.
\tag{11}
\]
For \(j\ne i\) with \(A_{ij}=1\), condition on all assignments except \(Z_j\).  The response change bound in (4) and the two-point calculation yield
\[
 |\mathbb E_Z[X_jY_i^{\mathrm{obs}}]|
 =\frac14\left|\mathbb E_Z[Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid Z_j=1]
 -\mathbb E_Z[Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid Z_j=0]\right|
 \leq\frac B{4N_i}.
\tag{12}
\]
If \(j\ne i\) and \(A_{ij}=0\), the expectation is zero by anonymous interference and assignment independence.  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \frac4n\sum_i\left|\sum_j(C_A)_{ij}\mathbb E_Z[X_jY_i^{\mathrm{obs}}]\right|
 &\leq\frac{2B}{n}\sum_i|(C_A)_{ii}|\\
 &\quad+\frac Bn\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j:A_{ij}=1}|(C_A)_{ij}|
 =\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]
Combining (10)--(13) with \({\rm def:target}\), \({\rm def:estimator}\), and \({\rm def:radii}\) proves
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z(\widehat\theta_h-\theta_n\mid A,(f_i)_i)\right|
 \leq\overline b_h(A).
\tag{14}
\]

Because \(P_A\) is a spectral projector of the symmetric matrix \(A\), it commutes with \(A\), so \(C_A=P_AA\) is symmetric.  If \(C_A=\sum_t\nu_tu_tu_t^\top\), orthonormality gives
\[
 \sum_i|(C_A)_{ii}|
 \leq\sum_t|\nu_t|\sum_i u_{t,i}^2=\sum_t|\nu_t|=\|C_A\|_*.
\tag{15}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz first within each positive-degree row and then across rows gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j:A_{ij}=1}|(C_A)_{ij}|
 &\leq\sum_{i:N_i>0}
 \left\{\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j:A_{ij}=1}(C_A)_{ij}^2\right\}^{1/2}\\
 &\leq\sqrt{nG_A(C_A)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{16}
\]
Substitution into the definition of \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}\) proves
\[
 \widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
 \leq\frac{2B}{n}\|C_A\|_*+B\sqrt{\frac{G_A(C_A)}n}.
\tag{17}
\]

Conditional Chebyshev applied to (8) and (14) gives
\[
 \Pr_Z\!\left(
 |\widehat\theta_h-\theta_n|>
 \overline b_h(A)+\frac{\overline s_h(A)}{\sqrt\alpha}
 \mathrel{\Big|}A,(f_i)_i\right)\leq\alpha.
\tag{18}
\]
When \(\overline s_h(A)=0\), (8) makes the centered fluctuation zero almost surely, so (18) remains valid.  The derivative envelope and \({\rm def:target}\) give \(|\theta_n|\leq B\); intersecting with \([-B,B]\) therefore cannot remove the target.  Integrating (18) proves uniform coverage.

Finally, for each realized degree the truncated score changes only when \(h\) crosses one of finitely many lattice distances, so there are at most \(n^2\) breakpoints over all units.  Exact finite binomial sums compute \(\mu_{2,i}(h)\), the finite maxima compute \(Q_{i,h}\) and \(D_{ij,h}\), one eigendecomposition computes \(C_A\), and matrix and finite-sum arithmetic compute the remaining certificates.  This is polynomial time.  By \({\rm lem:exact-score-hoeffding-projections}\), the first projection of \(q_h-4P_AAX\) is \(4(I_n-P_A)AX\) and its second projection is zero, with neither projection depending on \(h\).  Equations (8), (14), (17), and (18) prove every asserted certificate without imposing a sharper stochastic order.

\[
 g^{(2)}=\sum_{j<k}\left\{\mathbb E[g\mid X_j,X_k]
 -\mathbb E[g\mid X_j]-\mathbb E[g\mid X_k]\right\},
\]
and apply these definitions coordinatewise to a vector.  The first two conditional Hoeffding projections of the exact-support score satisfy
\[
 q_h^{(1)}=4AX,\qquad q_h^{(2)}=0
\]
simultaneously for every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\).  Consequently, for every \(A\)-measurable orthogonal projector \(\Pi\),
\[
 \{(I_n-\Pi)q_h\}^{(1)}=4(I_n-\Pi)AX,
 \qquad \{(I_n-\Pi)q_h\}^{(2)}=0,
\]

\[

\]

statements.proof_tex:
Condition on \(A\), and put \(X_j=Z_j-1/2\).  The score is centered by \({\rm lem:exact-score-moments}\).  Fix \(i\).  If \(A_{ij}=1\), the \(N_i\) neighbor contrasts are exchangeable.  Since
\[
 V_i=N_i^{-1}\sum_{k:A_{ik}=1}X_k,
\]
the exact first-moment identity in \({\rm lem:exact-score-moments}\) yields
\[
 1=\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i\mid A]
 =N_i^{-1}\sum_{k:A_{ik}=1}\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}X_k\mid A]
 =\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}X_j\mid A].
\]
If \(A_{ij}=0\), then \(q_{i,h}\) is independent of the centered variable \(X_j\), so the same covariance is zero.  Because \(\mathbb E_ZX_j^2=1/4\), the orthogonal projection of \(q_{i,h}\) onto the span of \(X_j\) is \(4A_{ij}X_j\).  Summing over \(j\) proves, coordinatewise and simultaneously for all admissible \(h\),
\[
 q_h^{(1)}=4AX.
\]

For the second projection, take distinct \(j,k\).  If either coordinate is not a neighbor of \(i\), independence makes the corresponding two-coordinate interaction zero.  If both are neighbors, integrate \(q_{i,h}\) over all contrasts except \((X_j,X_k)\).  Simultaneously changing every neighbor contrast to its negative preserves their joint law and changes the odd score to its negative.  The resulting conditional function on \(\{-1/2,1/2\}^2\) is therefore odd under \((X_j,X_k)\mapsto(-X_j,-X_k)\).  Its four-term Walsh expansion can contain only the degree-one monomials: the constant and the product \(X_jX_k\) are even under simultaneous sign reversal.  After subtracting the two first-coordinate projections, the \(\{j,k\}\) interaction is zero.  Hence
\[
 q_h^{(2)}=0.
\]

An \(A\)-measurable linear map preserves Hoeffding order.  Thus, for every \(A\)-measurable orthogonal projector \(\Pi\),
\[
 \{(I_n-\Pi)q_h\}^{(1)}=4(I_n-\Pi)AX,
 \qquad \{(I_n-\Pi)q_h\}^{(2)}=0.
\]
Finally, conditional independence under \({\rm ass:bernoulli-design}\) gives \(\mathbb E_Z[XX^\top\mid A]=I_n/4\).  Symmetry of \(A\) and idempotence of \(I_n-\Pi\) then imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_Z\!\left[\|4(I_n-\Pi)AX\|_2^2\mid A\right]
 &=16\operatorname{tr}\!\left((I_n-\Pi)AA^\top(I_n-\Pi)\frac{I_n}{4}\right)\\
 &=4\|(I_n-\Pi)A\|_{\mathrm F}^2.
\end{aligned}
\]

Let \(I_0(A)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}\).  Under the repaired class, any graph-only radius \(b(A)\) that is required to satisfy
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z(\widetilde\theta-\theta_n\mid A,(f_i)_i)\right|\leq b(A)
\]
for every response configuration in the conditional support must obey
\[
 b(A)\geq \frac{B}{n}I_0(A)
\]
on every realized graph.  Whenever \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) is nonempty, the independent-Rademacher response submodel \(f_i(a,x)=\varepsilon_iBx\) is admissible, and even a genie revealing every nonisolate sign leaves, conditionally on \(A\), Bayes absolute-error risk between
\[
 \frac{B}{\sqrt3\,n}\sqrt{I_0(A)}
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad
 \frac{B}{n}\sqrt{I_0(A)}.
\]
Thus the corresponding unconditional missing-sign fluctuation is of order \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E\sqrt{I_0(A)}\), which is no larger than the expected conditional radius \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E I_0(A)\).  This distinction neither constructs an unconditionally honest interval nor proves that every such interval must pay the graph-only conditional radius.
statements.justification: Opposite derivative signs on realized isolates give identical conditional observed laws, while an independent-sign calculation gives the exact square-root-count unconditional fluctuation scale.
statements.gap: The first conclusion is conditional on the graph and response configuration; it does not establish a sharp expected length for all unconditionally honest procedures.
statements.consumer: Analysts using the conditional certificate must retain the realized isolate allowance or explicitly change the inferential conditioning convention.
statements.proof_tex:
If \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) is empty, the assertion quantified over admissible laws is vacuous.  Suppose it is nonempty.  Retain the latent-type and graph law of one admissible member and replace only its response draw by
\[
 f_i(a,x)=\varepsilon_iBx,
 \qquad \varepsilon_i\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}{\rm Unif}\{-1,1\},
\tag{1}
\]
with signs independent of latent types, graph variables, and assignments.  The pairs \((U_i,f_i)\) remain independent and identically distributed with uniform \(U_i\)-marginal, as required by \({\rm ass:unit-sampling}\).  For every displayed argument,
\[
 |f_i(a,x)|\leq B,
 \qquad |\partial_xf_i(a,x)|=B,
 \qquad \partial_x^2f_i(a,x)=\partial_x^3f_i(a,x)=0.
\tag{2}
\]
Thus \({\rm ass:response-envelope}\) and \({\rm ass:third-derivative-bound}\) hold for every \(L\geq0\); all retained graph and randomization properties are unchanged, and \({\rm ass:anonymous-interference}\) supplies the potential outcomes.  Hence (1) is an admissible submodel.

Fix a graph \(A\) in the support of this submodel, and set
\[
 S_0(A)=\{i\in\mathcal V_n:N_i=0\},
 \qquad |S_0(A)|=I_0(A).
\tag{3}
\]
Take two sign vectors in the conditional support which agree on \(S_0(A)^c\), with all isolate signs equal to \(+1\) in the first and \(-1\) in the second.  Each vector has positive conditional probability.  If \(i\in S_0(A)\), anonymous interference and (1) give for every assignment
\[
 Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=f_i(Z_i,0)=0.
\tag{4}
\]
The nonisolate responses agree because their signs agree.  Therefore the complete conditional observed-data laws, and hence the conditional mean of any data-measurable estimator \(\widetilde\theta\), are identical under the two configurations.  Denote that common mean by \(m(A)\).  By \({\rm def:target}\),
\[
 \theta_n(\varepsilon)=\frac Bn\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\varepsilon_i,
 \qquad |\theta_n^+-\theta_n^-|=\frac{2B}{n}I_0(A).
\tag{5}
\]
If a graph-only radius \(b(A)\) bounds the absolute conditional bias for every response configuration in the conditional support, it bounds both \(|m(A)-\theta_n^+|\) and \(|m(A)-\theta_n^-|\).  Thus the triangle inequality gives
\[
 2b(A)\geq|m(A)-\theta_n^+|+|m(A)-\theta_n^-|
 \geq|\theta_n^+-\theta_n^-|=\frac{2B}{n}I_0(A),
\]
which proves \(b(A)\geq BI_0(A)/n\) on every realized graph in the support.

For the Bayes calculation, reveal \(A\) and all signs on \(S_0(A)^c\).  Conditional on this genie information, the known nonisolate part of the target can be subtracted.  By independence in (1) and the zero observations in (4), all remaining data are independent of
\[
 T_0(A)=\frac Bn\sum_{i\in S_0(A)}\varepsilon_i.
\tag{6}
\]
Thus, writing \(K=I_0(A)\) and \(S_K=\sum_{k=1}^K\varepsilon_k\), the conditional genie Bayes absolute-error risk is
\[
 \frac Bn\inf_{a\in\mathbb R}\mathbb E|S_K-a|.
\]
The law of \(S_K\) is symmetric, and \((|s-a|+|-s-a|)/2\geq|s|\); averaging proves that zero is a Bayes action.  Hence the risk equals \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E|S_K|\).  Independence and centering give
\[
 \mathbb ES_K^2=K,
 \qquad \mathbb ES_K^4=K+6{K\choose2}=3K^2-2K\leq3K^2.
\tag{7}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz yields \(\mathbb E|S_K|\leq\sqrt K\).  H\"older's inequality gives
\[
 K=\mathbb ES_K^2
 \leq(\mathbb E|S_K|)^{2/3}(\mathbb E|S_K|^4)^{1/3},
 \qquad \mathbb E|S_K|\geq\sqrt{K/3}.
\tag{8}
\]
The same inequalities hold at \(K=0\).  Substitution of \(K=I_0(A)\) proves the displayed conditional Bayes-risk bounds.  Averaging over \(A\) gives unconditional scale \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E\sqrt{I_0(A)}\); since \(\sqrt K\leq K\) for every nonnegative integer \(K\), it is no larger than \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb EI_0(A)\).  This argument neither constructs an unconditionally honest interval nor lower-bounds every such interval, establishing the final scope qualification.

The paper develops design-based asymptotic theory under Bernoulli assignment for Horvitz--Thompson estimators of direct, indirect, and total average treatment effects under uniformly bounded neighbourhood interference, and proposes eigenvector-adjusted point estimators and variance estimators. In contrast, the present note uses a stochastic sparse-graphon model, targets a midpoint derivative on exact realized-degree lattices, proves a finite-sample graph-observable conditional certificate, and gives a same-class smoothness-dependent minimax expected-length lower benchmark without proving a matching feasible upper rate.

tldr: A Bernoulli network experiment reveals a derivative only through the exact binomial support associated with each realized degree. The proposal studies the new finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) in the known-rank sparse-graphon model, uses \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\) so every positive degree has a normalized local score, and reports a graph-observable interval radius containing exact degree-level bias, exact inverse score moments, the graph dependence term, isolates, and feasible-PC remainders. The supported-unit frontier retains lattice, interior, and graph-floor phases. A same-class testing calculation gives only \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\) for isolates, whereas the safe interval pays \(B\pi_{0,n}\); therefore no full matched-frontier theorem is claimed. The open content is uniform feasible-PC certification and tail-adaptive completion without minimum-degree or response-sharing assumptions. Li and Wager's Theorem 6 is used only through an explicit finite-to-derivative bridge as an asymptotic benchmark.

project_justification.gap: Li and Wager prove asymptotic normality for a PC estimator of their finite and population indirect effects, but they do not give finite-sample honest length for the distinct realized derivative target or handle exact low-degree support. Standard honest nonparametric theory has no random exposure lattice, graph projector, or latent-type-dependent isolate tail.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a degree-exact, bias-aware statistical frontier for a causal derivative from one network, with observable support diagnostics and an honest distinction between conservative isolate bias and the same-class testing modulus.
project_justification.fill: The project derives exact score moments at every positive degree, proves a finite-sample bridge to the published indirect effect, constructs PC-balanced observable radii, establishes supported-unit upper and lower rates plus a degree-tail modulus, and isolates the one remaining tail-adaptation question instead of asserting a false matched frontier.

related_work: LiWager2022RandomGraph is the central asymptotic benchmark. Proposition 1, equations (4)--(5), relates its finite indirect effect to an average derivative through a minimum-degree remainder, and Theorem 6, equation (43), gives a \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\)-scale Gaussian limit for its PC estimator in a polynomial-degree sparse regime. The present target \(\theta_n\) is a new realized finite-population derivative; \({\rm prop:li-wager-bridge}\) gives the exact degree-level comparison, so no finite-sample same-target tightening is claimed. HuLiWager2022AverageDirectIndirect supplies the Bernoulli-policy decomposition and causal interpretation. ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest informs the computable smoothness-bias interval geometry, while CaiLow2004Adaptation informs the testing-to-expected-length argument; neither treats network support or spectral residualization. AbbeFanWangZhong2020Entrywise and TangCape2025InfiniteRank inform the empirical-eigenspace analysis but do not control an exact-support causal score. Leung2022NetworkInference concerns locality-based inference for level effects. BhadraSchweinberger2025Survey is cited only as a broad survey of network-interference frameworks; the separate arXiv identifier 2504.06108 is omitted because its current contagion manuscript is not the linear-rate comparator described in the earlier core.
technical_internal_limitation: For \(N_i>0\), the exact score has second moment \(\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}\) and third-order bias at most \(Lh_i(h)^2/6\).
